title: The Long Forgotten Classroom Management Strategy You Need
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin diagnoses chronically attention-seeking, 'needy' students as products of learned helplessness -- adults in their lives having rewarded constant demands for help and attention -- rather than intentional misbehavior, and proposes two SCM strategies to reverse the pattern. First, strict adherence to a hand-raising, ask-permission classroom management plan physically limits a needy student's ability to follow the teacher around or blurt out constantly, creating a pause that forces self-reliance. Second, and more fundamentally, is a persistent push for independence: withholding help unless a student genuinely lacks the needed information, and using short phrases of encouragement ('You got this,' 'You don't need me') instead of solving problems for them. He argues the combined effect over a few weeks is a visible jump in maturity, confidence, and academic ability, particularly for students previously locked into learned helplessness.
points: Needy, attention-seeking behavior is framed as learned helplessness reinforced by adults, not an inherent trait, and therefore reversible.
A strict hand-raising, ask-permission structure limits a needy student's physical and verbal access to the teacher, forcing them to problem-solve first.
Withhold help unless a student is truly missing needed information, replacing assistance with brief encouragement like 'You got this' or 'Go back and read it again.'
Consistent independence-building is presented as reliably improving confidence, behavior, and academic ability within a matter of weeks.
quotes: They get their way by never taking no for an answer. They’ve discovered that the squeaky-wheel strategy works.
But when you rely on others to an unhealthy degree every little thing becomes a big deal. A hangnail needs a band-aid.
You’ll never, ever provide help unless they’re without the information they need do it themselves.
Force them to rely on their own wits until they realize it’s futile to ask you and that they can indeed trust their own judgment.
They’ll become different people in a few weeks. They’ll stand taller. They’ll speak clearer and deeper.
